lane: A2 — carried shape across the BUILD→FIGHT transition soft-locks free-form building for the rest of the match
owner_item: He was mid-drag with a shape pulled out of his castle when the FIGHT whistle blew; the shape stayed glued to his cursor, he could not place it and could not let go of it, and for the rest of the match every further free-form pickup was refused as though he were still holding something — while towers, upgrades and the castle panel all kept working.
root_cause:
THE SOFT-LOCK AND ITS TOTAL ABSENCE OF AN EXIT ARE CONFIRMED IN CODE. THE PRECISE EVENT THAT LOST HIS DROP IS NARROWED TO THREE PROVABLE CANDIDATES, NOT ONE.

`player.kind` is a discriminated union in authoritative, wire-carried world state (`src/game/player.ts:188-192`: `CarryingPlayer = PlayerCommon & { readonly kind: 'Carrying'; readonly carriedSparkId: SparkId }`). The whole soft-lock is one line — `src/input/controls.ts:1063`:

    if (player?.kind === 'Idle' && player.carriedPotatoId === undefined) {

Every world pick in `onDown` — gatherer re-task, bomb, rainbow, potato, and `pickSpark` → `PICKUP_SPARK` — lives inside that block. While the world says `Carrying`, no new free-form gesture can ever begin. That is, word for word, his *"it kind of counted like I already have a shape on me"*. The character card was deliberately hoisted OUT of that block in S182, which is exactly why he could still click sheets, towers and upgrades while free-form was dead.

**Nothing ever clears `Carrying` except a local pointer edge.** The complete set of `DROP_SPARK` producers on the human path is `controls.ts:1439` (inside `onUp`, nested in `this.state.kind === 'AttractDrag'` AND the `mine` guard at `:1438`), `controls.ts:1537` (`onLostCapture`), and `controlsCore.ts:98` (bench only). There is no per-frame reconciler, no key, no timeout, no phase action, and the spark itself never expires (`physicsLoop.ts:294` reaps only `s.state.kind === 'Free'`, and `applyDespawnSpark` no-ops on non-Free). So ONE lost, skipped or refused `DROP_SPARK` is permanent for the match.

**And the defensive code that was meant to cover the anomaly is what makes it look welded on.** `src/input/controlsCore.ts:119-127`:

    if (player.kind === 'Carrying' && state.kind !== 'AttractDrag') {
      const carried = world.freeSparks.get(player.carriedSparkId);
      if (carried !== undefined) { carried.pos.x = cursor.x; carried.pos.y = cursor.y; ... }

Carrying-with-no-gesture is *rendered* forever — the shape is pinned to his cursor every substep — instead of being *recovered from*. This runs on the joiner too (`main.ts:2749`), so it produces his *"it was just stuck with me the whole game"* on either seat.

THE THREE WAYS THE DROP GOES MISSING, all read in code:
(1) `controlsCore.ts:109-111` — `if (!mine) { return { kind: 'Idle' }; }` ends the gesture and dispatches NOTHING. The next `onUp` then fails its `this.state.kind === 'AttractDrag'` gate, so no drop ever fires.
(2) `main.ts:588` — `if (migrationPauseActive) return;` swallows a `DROP_SPARK` entirely: no optimistic apply, no wire send, no retry.
(3) `net/hostHandlers.ts:312-315` — an empty per-peer token bucket `return`s on any INTENT, `DROP_SPARK` included. The joiner has already predicted itself Idle (`DROP_SPARK` is in `PREDICTABLE_ACTIONS`, `main.ts:527`), so the next host snapshot restores `Carrying` and the local gesture is already gone.

WHAT IS *NOT* THE CAUSE, checked and cleared so nobody re-opens them: `applyPlaceFromFree` is genuinely atomic — `canBuildNow` is at `placeFromFree.ts:173`, `fsmPickup` at `:222`, so the S52 stuck-Carrying defect is already fixed there. `depositIntoCastle` is escrow-guarded and `applyPickupSpark` clears `spark.escrow` (`sparkLifecycle.ts:167`), so a gatherer cannot delete a shape out of his hand. `eligiblePorchSparks` filters `state.kind === 'Free'`, so a tower stamp cannot spend it either.

ON HIS QUESTION 2 — THERE IS NO BUILD→FIGHT CARRY-RETURN PATH, AND THERE NEVER WAS. `hostTick.ts:401-503` is the entire phase-edge block and it has exactly one arm, `if (world.matchPhase === 'BUILD')`. Nothing at all fires on entry to FIGHT. But the behaviour he remembers is REAL and he described it accurately — it is `enforceSpawnerBounds` (`game/spawner.ts:461-480`), which rim-snaps any un-escrowed Free spark back inside the quarry disc every substep. So *"the shape goes back to the center, it doesn't even go back to your tower"* is what happens the instant a drop LANDS, at any time in the match. It is not a transition handler; it is the consequence of the drop. His memory is right, his model of where it lives is wrong, and that distinction is the fix.

FINALLY, ONE HALF OF HIS REPORT IS CORRECT BEHAVIOUR AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED": `buildLegality.ts:47` refuses all placement outside BUILD, and `phaseSplit.test.ts:20` records the ruling as *"Nothing is buildable outside BUILD, at every gate"* — his own S149 bug report was that the split did NOT exist. So *"I couldn't place it"* is correct for the 45 s of FIGHT. What is broken is that he could not LET GO, and that the lock outlived the fight.

fix_shape:
TWO HALVES. (a) IS LOAD-BEARING FOR *THIS* BUG; (b) IS WHAT STOPS THE NEXT ONE, AND IT IS CHEAPER.

⭐ ARGUED: (b) IS ACTUALLY THE MORE LOAD-BEARING OF THE TWO, AND THE BRIEF SHOULD SAY SO. A FIGHT-edge clear fixes precisely the transition he hit. But the carry is stranded by lost intents, migration pauses and `!mine` gesture cancels that have nothing to do with the clock — and until the next BUILD→FIGHT edge (up to 135 s away) he is still locked. (b) recovers within a frame from ALL of them, including the three entry paths above. Ship both; if only one can land, land (b).

(b1) MAKE THE DROP TOTAL — `src/state/sparkLifecycle.ts`, ~4 lines. In `applyDropSpark`, replace `if (spark === undefined) throw new Error('carried spark missing')` with: if the spark is gone, still `world.players.set(player.id, fsmDrop(player))` and return. A carry whose spark has vanished is a bug in whoever deleted it, but refusing to release the PLAYER converts it into a match-long lock. Keep the `player.kind !== 'Carrying'` CarryViolation throw — that one is a genuine caller error and `onLostCapture` already guards it.

(b2) SELF-HEAL THE ORPHANED CARRY — `src/input/controlsCore.ts`, ~8 lines. Invert the `Carrying && state.kind !== 'AttractDrag'` branch at :119: instead of pinning the spark to the cursor, dispatch `DROP_SPARK` at the cursor and leave the state Idle. Post-S52 the ONLY producer of `Carrying` on the human path is `PICKUP_SPARK` in `onDown`, which enters `AttractDrag` in the same statement (`controls.ts:1140-1148`), so on the local seat this combination has no legitimate meaning. ⚠ HAZARD TO CHECK FIRST: this function is shared by `Controls.applyPerSubstep` and the worker facade (`state/workerSim.ts:152`), and it runs on the joiner's MIRROR every frame (`main.ts:2749`) as well as the host. Verify it is only ever called with the LOCAL seat's playerId before letting it dispatch — a bot seat legitimately holds `Carrying` with no AttractDrag (`botController.ts:172-183`). If that cannot be established cheaply, put the identical self-heal in `Controls.applyPerSubstep` (the class layer, which is unambiguously local-seat) instead of the shared core.

(b3) UNCONDITIONAL RELEASE ON `onUp` — `src/input/controls.ts`, ~6 lines. Today the drop at :1439 is nested inside `this.state.kind === 'AttractDrag'` and `mine`. Add, at the top of the `e.button === 0` arm, the same shape `onLostCapture` already uses at :1536: if `player?.kind === 'Carrying'`, dispatch `DROP_SPARK` — full stop. Safe only once (b1) has landed, which is why (b1) goes first.

(a) THE FIGHT EDGE CLEARS EVERY CARRY — `src/state/hostTick.ts`, ~12 lines. Add the missing `else` arm at :502 (`if (world.matchPhase === 'FIGHT')`), iterating seats in SORTED ID ORDER (the file's own `tickGathererShelter` precedent at `gathererLifecycle.ts:637`, never raw `Map` order), and for each `kind === 'Carrying'` seat dispatch `DROP_SPARK` at the carried spark's current position. `enforceSpawnerBounds` then does the rest for free on the next substep and the shape rim-snaps to the quarry — which is EXACTLY the behaviour he described as normal, achieved with no new "return to centre" code. Host-authoritative, so it reaches every seat including joiners and bots via the snapshot.

⛔ WHAT NOT TO DO: do not relax `canBuildNow`'s phase gate (`buildLegality.ts:47`) — building during FIGHT is his own S149 ruling, pinned by `phaseSplit.test.ts`. Do not touch `placeFromFree.ts` — its ordering is already correct. Do not add a `carryStuckSinceTick` or any new Player field; it would re-open all four sites and force a protocol bump for a bug that needs neither.
determinism_risk:
YES — THE (a) HALF IS INSIDE THE SIM. Named hazards:

1. MAP ITERATION ORDER. The FIGHT-edge sweep walks `world.players`, whose iteration is seat-INSERTION order and can legitimately differ between a host and a rehydrating mirror (`stateHashFull.ts:509-511` says exactly this about the same Map). Sort by seat id before dispatching, per `tickGathererShelter`'s precedent (`gathererLifecycle.ts:637-639`). The release also WRITES `spark.state`, `spark.pos`, `spark.prevPos` and `spark.createdTick` (`applyDropSpark`, sparkLifecycle.ts:219-229), and `freeSparks` IS in `NARROW_HASHED_FAMILIES` (`stateHash.ts:89`) — so a different order across sims is a real, hashed divergence, not a cosmetic one.

2. NO `Math.random`, NO WALL CLOCK, NO FLOAT ACCUMULATOR. The sweep is keyed on the existing `flipped` boolean, which is pure `world.tick` arithmetic (`hostTick.ts:386`). Add nothing time-based. The (b2) self-heal is likewise structural (`player.kind` + a `freeSparks` lookup), no tick math at all.

3. ⛔ DOUBLE-APPLY HAZARD IN (b2). `applyControlsPerSubstep` runs on the host's authoritative sim (`physicsLoop.ts:229`), on the worker-mode MIRROR (`main.ts:2722`) and on the joiner's mirror (`main.ts:2749`). Making it DISPATCH rather than merely mutate means a mirror would now originate an action. On the joiner that is correct (it is the same optimistic-predict-then-send path `onUp` already uses). In `?worker=1` mode it posts an intent to the worker, which is also the established posture. But this must be reasoned about explicitly, not assumed — and it is the reason the fallback (put the self-heal in `Controls.applyPerSubstep`, the unambiguously local-seat class layer) is offered.

4. FOUR SITES — DISCHARGED BY ADDING NO FIELD. `kind`/`carriedSparkId` already exist at all four: factory (`player.ts:238-289`, `pickup`/`drop`), serialize (`save.ts:2018` out, `save.ts:1874` in), hash (deliberately EXCLUDED — `stateHashFull.ts:174`, and absent from `NARROW_HASHED_FAMILIES`), worker (`workerSim.ts` runs the shared `controlsCore`). ⚠ The instant anyone adds a new Player field to track this, all four re-open and the hash exclusion becomes a live blind spot.

5. PROTOCOL_VERSION — NO BUMP. Currently **47** (`net/protocol.ts`; note CLAUDE.md still says 46, SPARK_CANON.md §6 is correct at 47). The fix adds no serialized field, removes none, and introduces no new discriminant value on an existing action. `DROP_SPARK` is already in both allowlists (`protocol.ts:1417` KNOWN_GAME_ACTION_TYPES, `:1542` CLIENT_INTENT_TYPES) and 'allow' in both gates (`benchGate.ts:52`, `elimination.ts:112`). The wire shape is unchanged, so a v47 peer needs no knowledge of the fix.
tests_owed:
⚠ NO RENDERER AND NO `Controls` INSTANCE RUNS UNDER VITEST. `src/input/controls.test.ts:3-6` states it outright — the class binds canvas/window listeners in its constructor and cannot be built in node. So `onDown`/`onUp`/`onLostCapture` are NOT unit-testable, and every assertion has to land on a pure export or a reducer. Plan accordingly.

1. `src/state/sparkLifecycle.test.ts` — construct a world with a seat in `Carrying` whose `carriedSparkId` is absent from `freeSparks`, dispatch `DROP_SPARK`. TODAY: throws `carried spark missing`. AFTER: returns, seat is `Idle`. This is the one-line proof that a stuck carry can always be released.

2. `src/state/phaseSplit.test.ts` — the file that already owns "the phase edge does X" and already imports `runHostTick`, `makeHostTickState` and `PHASE_DURATION_TICKS`. Add: seat carrying a spark, drive `runHostTick` across the BUILD→FIGHT boundary, assert (i) `players.get(P0).kind === 'Idle'`, (ii) the spark is back to `state.kind === 'Free'`, (iii) after one `stepPhysics` it is inside `SPAWNER_RADIUS` — i.e. it really did go back to the centre, pinned against `enforceSpawnerBounds` rather than against prose. TODAY all three fail; there is no FIGHT arm at all.

3. `src/state/phaseSplit.test.ts` (second case) — the double-flip. The edge block is guarded on `flipped`, and a NONET freeze can cross two boundaries in one evaluation (`hostTick.ts:396-400`). Assert the carry is still released when the loop lands on FIGHT after two flips. This is the exact class the file's own comment says a before/after diff would miss.

4. `src/input/controls.test.ts` — extend `applyControlsPerSubstep` coverage (it is already an export via `controls.ts:70`): a `Carrying` player with `state.kind === 'Idle'` must emit `DROP_SPARK` into the captured dispatch fn instead of writing `carried.pos`. Assert the NEGATIVE too — a `Carrying` player mid-`AttractDrag` must NOT drop, or every drag dies on frame one.

5. ⭐ THE SOFT-LOCK ITSELF HAS NO UNIT TEST AND CANNOT GET ONE, because `controls.ts:1063` only exists inside the un-instantiable class. It must be pinned by e2e: `e2e/match-clock.spec.ts` already drives the clock and is in the `e2e:gating` lane. Add — grab a shape, cross the FIGHT edge mid-drag, release, then assert a SECOND pickup succeeds. Without this the headline symptom is untested at every level. ⚠ If a NEW spec file is created instead of extending this one, `src/ci.e2eLanes.test.ts` pins the spec→lane mapping and goes red until it is updated.

6. REGRESSION GUARD, cheap and worth it: assert `applyPlaceFromFree` on a FIGHT-phase world leaves the seat `Idle` and the spark `Free` (`placeFromFree.test.ts` exists). It passes today — that is the point. It stops a future session "fixing" the atomic path and re-introducing S52.
owner_ruling_needed: WHERE DOES THE SHAPE GO WHEN THE WHISTLE TAKES IT OFF HIM? He answered this himself in the same breath — *"the shape goes back to the center. It doesn't even go back to your tower, it goes back to the center, which is fine for now"* — so the brief ships option (i) and does not block on him. (i) BACK TO THE QUARRY CENTRE: costs literally zero new code, because dropping an un-escrowed spark makes `enforceSpawnerBounds` rim-snap it into the disc on the next substep. Consequence: a shape his gatherer walked to the keep and he paid a pull for is returned to the SHARED quarry, where an opponent's gatherer can take it. (ii) BACK INTO HIS CASTLE BANK: ~3 extra lines (`bankAdd(world.castleBanks, seat, spark.type)` then delete the entity, mirroring `depositIntoCastle` at `gathererLifecycle.ts:172-177`), and it is the option that matches what he actually paid for — it is also exactly what the gatherer shelter already does with ITS cargo one second earlier at the same edge (`tickGathererShelter`, `gathererLifecycle.ts:646-651`), so (i) makes the player's shape and his gatherer's shape behave differently at the same whistle. THE CASE FOR ASKING: his "which is fine for now" is permission, not a preference, and (ii) is both cheaper than it looks and more internally consistent. ONE QUESTION, ANSWERABLE IN A WORD.

NOT A RULING, A NOTICE HE SHOULD HAVE: he will still be unable to place a free-form shape for the 45 s of every FIGHT, and that is HIS OWN S149 RULING, not a leftover bug — `phaseSplit.test.ts:20` records it as *"Nothing is buildable outside BUILD, at every gate"*, written against his report that no split existed. After this fix he will be able to LET GO mid-fight and keep playing; he will still not be able to BUILD mid-fight. If that second half is what he actually wanted changed, that is a separate, much larger scope item and needs its own brief — do not fold it into this one.
size_estimate: Standard (10-30K). Four production files but each edit is small (~4/8/6/12 lines); the cost is in the four test files, the e2e spec, and the one hazard that must be reasoned about rather than assumed — whether `applyControlsPerSubstep` may originate a dispatch given that it runs on the host sim, the worker mirror and the joiner mirror.
blocked_on: NOTHING. Both halves are specified and the owner's own words already authorise the centre-return default ("which is fine for now"); the bank-return alternative is a one-word improvement, not a gate. A live-session read of `world.diagnostics.intentThrottled` would confirm or eliminate entry path #3, but the fix does not depend on which of the three fired — all three are recovered by the same (b) self-heal.
